subject.title: Preserve aborted sessions across restart opt-in

question: Should OpenClaw accept `session.restartContinuation` as a new core config contract for aborted main-session continuity, or require a different restart-recovery design?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but the permanent product/API choice affects config surface, upgrade expectations, and session-state semantics rather than being a purely mechanical defect fix.

options.title: Close Until Sponsored
options.body: Close this PR now and let a maintainer reopen or sponsor a fresh branch if the opt-in config contract is accepted.

options.title: Sponsor Opt-In Config
options.body: A maintainer explicitly accepts the new `session.restartContinuation` contract and owns the compatibility/session-state risk before merge.

options.title: Request Config-Free Recovery
options.body: Ask for a replacement design that fixes the continuity gap through existing restart recovery behavior without adding this config knob.

recommendation.title: Close Until Sponsored
recommendation.body: Close this PR now and let a maintainer reopen or sponsor a fresh branch if the opt-in config contract is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest adjacent maintainer signal on the broader graceful-restart scope and restart drain behavior.
